about: Wonders tour (wonders.js): curated stops round the Earth. Camera: lat/lon = the point looked at; altKm = camera distance from the ground there (km); pitch = tilt from straight down (deg, 0 = map view); heading = compass direction the camera faces (deg, 0 = north). The phone profile scales these in wonders.js (×1.35 distance, ×0.85 tilt) unless a stop has its own 'phone' {altKm, pitch}. 'data' says honestly what the globe can show there. Every 'line' is checked against the listed source (see review/wonders/facts-check.md).

stops.name: The Alps · Mont Blanc
stops.line: Mont Blanc is the top of the Alps: about 4,806 m, and its icy summit changes height a little with every survey.
stops.data: Land relief from Copernicus DEM; heights are exaggerated so the shape reads.
stops.source: Haute-Savoie surveyors' 2023 measurement, 4,805.59 m (reported by Reuters, 6 Oct 2023)

stops.name: Norway's fjords · Sognefjord
stops.line: Glaciers carved the Sognefjord: about 205 km long and over 1,300 m deep, far deeper than the sea outside it.
stops.data: Fjord floor from EMODnet survey bathymetry where covered, else GEBCO.
stops.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Sogne Fjord' (204 km long, 1,308 m deep)

stops.name: Iceland
stops.line: Iceland sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge: the North American and Eurasian plates pull apart right through it, about 2 cm a year.
stops.data: Land relief and the GEBCO sea floor round the island.
stops.source: USGS, 'Understanding plate motions' (This Dynamic Earth); Icelandic Met Office

stops.name: Mid-Atlantic Ridge
stops.line: The longest mountain range on Earth is under the sea: the ridge runs down the whole Atlantic, and its two sides spread about 2.5 cm a year.
stops.data: Sea floor from the GEBCO grid (~460 m): the ridge and its fracture zones are real; fine detail is not.
stops.source: NOAA Ocean Exploration, 'What is the mid-ocean ridge?' and 'Mid-Atlantic Ridge' facts

stops.name: Hossegor · La Gravière
stops.line: A deep undersea canyon, the Gouf de Capbreton, starts only a few hundred metres off the beach here and changes how swell arrives at Hossegor's sandbars.
stops.data: Canyon from EMODnet survey bathymetry; the sandbars move and are not in the data.
stops.source: Tourisme Landes, 'Le Gouf de Capbreton'; Mazières et al. 2014, Marine Geology 351 (canyon head geometry)

stops.name: Guéthary · Parlementia
stops.line: Parlementia is a reef break: the wave stands up over a rock shelf offshore, so it only wakes up with big swell.
stops.data: Sea floor from EMODnet survey bathymetry; open the spot for the reef model.
stops.source: Surf-Forecast, 'Parlementia' break guide (surf-forecast.com/breaks/Parlementia)

stops.name: Nazaré canyon
stops.line: Europe's largest undersea canyon starts just off Praia do Norte; it helps focus swell into the biggest wave ever surfed, 26.2 m, in 2020.
stops.data: Canyon from EMODnet survey bathymetry (~115 m).
stops.source: Guinness World Records 2022 (Sebastian Steudtner, 26.21 m, ride of 29 Oct 2020); Tyler et al. 2009, Oceanography 22(1), 'Europe's Grand Canyon: Nazaré submarine canyon'

stops.name: Peniche · Supertubos
stops.line: Peniche was an island until sand joined it to the mainland; Supertubos is the beach on that sand bridge.
stops.data: Real 2011 lidar reef here; open the spot for reef-scale detail.
stops.source: Câmara Municipal de Peniche history; Encyclopaedia Britannica 'Peniche'

stops.name: The Dead Sea
stops.line: The lowest land on Earth: the shore is more than 430 m below sea level, and the water drops about a metre a year.
stops.data: Land relief; the lake is drawn at its surface, not its floor.
stops.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica 'Dead Sea'; Geological Survey of Israel

stops.name: The Red Sea
stops.line: An ocean being born: Africa and Arabia are pulling apart down the middle of the Red Sea, which is why it is long, narrow and deep.
stops.data: Sea floor from the GEBCO grid; its coral reefs are smaller than the grid.
stops.source: USGS, This Dynamic Earth ('Red Sea' rift); Encyclopaedia Britannica 'Red Sea'

stops.name: Kilimanjaro
stops.line: Africa's highest mountain, 5,895 m, is a volcano standing alone on the plain, with snow near the equator.
stops.data: Land relief from Copernicus DEM.
stops.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica 'Kilimanjaro'; Tanzania National Parks

stops.name: Maldives atolls
stops.line: About 1,190 coral islands in rings called atolls; most of the land is only a metre or two above the sea.
stops.data: Honest note: the islands and reefs are smaller than the ~460 m GEBCO grid. You see the shallow atoll plateau, not the islands.
stops.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Maldives'

stops.name: Himalaya · Everest
stops.line: Everest is the highest point above sea level: 8,849 m, measured by Nepal and China together in 2020.
stops.data: Land relief from Copernicus DEM; heights exaggerated so the shape reads.
stops.source: Survey Department of Nepal and China joint announcement, 8 Dec 2020 (8,848.86 m)

stops.name: Lake Baikal
stops.line: The deepest lake on Earth, 1,642 m, holds about a fifth of all the unfrozen fresh water at the planet's surface.
stops.data: The lake is drawn at its surface; its floor is not in the data.
stops.source: UNESCO World Heritage 'Lake Baikal' (754); Encyclopaedia Britannica (1,642 m)

stops.name: Mariana Trench
stops.line: The deepest point in any ocean, the Challenger Deep: about 10,900 m down. Everest would fit inside with 2 km to spare.
stops.data: Sea floor from the GEBCO grid (~460 m); the trench's narrow bottom looks a little shallower here than it is.
stops.source: NOAA Ocean Exploration; Stewart & Jamieson 2019 (Earth-Science Reviews), 10,925 m ± 12 m

stops.name: Great Barrier Reef
stops.line: The largest coral reef system on Earth: about 2,300 km long, made of nearly 3,000 separate reefs.
stops.data: Honest note: single reefs are smaller than the ~460 m GEBCO grid. You see the wide continental shelf they grow on and its steep edge.
stops.source: Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority (gbrmpa.gov.au), 'Reef facts'

stops.name: Antarctica's ice
stops.line: Antarctica's ice sheet holds about 90 percent of the ice on Earth's surface and is on average about 2 km thick.
stops.data: The relief is the top of the ice; the rock under it is not shown.
stops.source: NSIDC 'Ice sheets' (nsidc.org/learn/parts-cryosphere/ice-sheets); Australian Antarctic Division

stops.name: Patagonia · Fitz Roy
stops.line: Granite spires on the edge of the Southern Patagonian Ice Field, the largest stretch of ice in the Southern Hemisphere outside Antarctica.
stops.data: Land relief (the ice field's surface) from Copernicus DEM.
stops.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica 'Patagonia' and 'Fitz Roy'; NASA Earth Observatory

stops.name: Andes · Aconcagua
stops.line: The Andes are the longest mountain range on land, and Aconcagua, 6,961 m, is the highest peak outside Asia.
stops.data: Land relief from Copernicus DEM.
stops.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica 'Aconcagua' and 'Andes'

stops.name: Grand Canyon
stops.line: The Colorado River cut this canyon: 446 km long and about 1.8 km deep, through rocks up to almost 2 billion years old.
stops.data: Land relief from Copernicus DEM.
stops.source: US National Park Service, Grand Canyon 'Park statistics' and geology pages

stops.name: The Rockies · Mount Elbert
stops.line: Mount Elbert, 4,401 m, is the highest peak of the Rocky Mountains, which run about 4,800 km from Canada to New Mexico.
stops.data: Land relief from Copernicus DEM.
stops.source: USGS (Mount Elbert 14,440 ft); Encyclopaedia Britannica 'Rocky Mountains'

stops.name: Monterey Canyon
stops.line: It starts right off the beach at Moss Landing and drops to more than 3,000 m: a canyon the size of the Grand Canyon, under the sea.
stops.data: Sea floor from survey bathymetry (California) where covered, else GEBCO.
stops.source: MBARI and NOAA Monterey Bay National Marine Sanctuary, 'Monterey Canyon'

stops.name: Hawaiian–Emperor seamounts
stops.line: A hot spot under the moving Pacific Plate drew this line of volcanoes: youngest at Hawaiʻi, older to the north-west, the bend about 47 million years old.
stops.data: Sea floor from the GEBCO grid: the seamounts are real, their fine shape is not.
stops.source: USGS, This Dynamic Earth 'Hotspots'; Sharp & Clague 2006 (Science), bend ~47 Ma

stops.name: Pipeline · Oʻahu
stops.line: North Pacific winter swells cross thousands of km of open ocean and hit this shallow reef with little shelf to slow them.
stops.data: Real 2013 lidar reef here; open the spot for reef-scale detail.
stops.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Banzai Pipeline'
